complexity_ledger.narrative:
specs/results/scorecards/score-drives-validation/GOAL-scored-at-goal-time/SV-06/RESULT.md is the evidence ledger and `references/goal_score_wiring.md` is the design.
WHAT WAS MEASURED. Over every `ticket_plan.yaml` on disk at `a527305`, live and sealed: 27 distinct epic goals, 12 of which name a scorecard dimension in prose, and ZERO whose `baseline.evidence` points at a sealed `scorecard.json` -- against 87 sealed cards in the record. The epic's own baseline says "NO GOAL HAS EVER BEEN KEYED TO A DIMENSION"; that clause is false (SV-06-DF-01) and the true gap is sharper: a goal here has DESCRIBED a score twelve times and has never BEEN one.
THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE, RUN AND REJECTED. An optional `scored_by:` block on `epic_goals[]` plus a `score_signal:` on the ticket-goal link was added to a scratch copy of this epic's plan and put through `git-epic-workflow/scripts/validate_epic_plan.py`: exit 0, byte-identical message, zero lines of Python changed, because the plan schema reads named fields and ignores unknown ones. It is REJECTED anyway -- every field is already sayable in `harness`, `metric` and `baseline.evidence`, and `dimension:` would export an index into one project's rubric into a schema three skills share. Cheap to add is not a reason to add. The experiment is sealed at validator-experiment/ because it is the argument AGAINST the field, and because its other half is the absence guarantee: a plan with no scoring block validates today, unchanged, and will validate identically after SV-07.
ALSO REJECTED: scoring at ticket start or ticket close (cost, rubric noise exceeding one ticket's movement, and R-H1/R-H2 comparability against a mid-epic tree); any new check or gate, including a check that a judged goal carries a card baseline (`no_new_gates_rule` -- 0 of 27 argues for a sentence, not a checker); a `--goal` flag on `score_tools.py` or any `tla-spec-dev` path that reads a plan, which would invert the dependency and make the card a participant in the goal process rather than an instrument it names; and a shared "judged instrument" reference page in any skill, which would be a seventh file in a surface this ticket had just finished counting.
WHAT THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS. A THIRD suite red is inherited and the epic lists only two. `tests/test_card_has_one_home.py::test_only_the_card_states_a_dimension_an_anchor_or_a_scoring_rule` fails on four lines in `SCORE-DRIVES-VALIDATION-EPIC.md` and `specs/desired_program_model/ticket_plan.yaml` -- the only two files `a527305` touched, in the same document that says "Two reds are inherited deliberately". Demonstrated inherited, not caused: with this ticket's page, evidence tree and findings all removed, the failure is identical, and SV-06's own design page appears nowhere in the offender list. NOT FILED -- the finding budget of 5 is spent and none of the five is blocking; escalated in RESULT.md section 7 and the ticket report, per RM-02's precedent. NOT REPAIRED -- both files are outside this ticket's implementation scope and silently repairing an inherited red is forbidden.
BYTE COST: zero. Nothing here touches `references/eval_scorecard.md`, so `serve` stays 6,281 bytes and 9 rungs, and the SV-07 hand-off creates no anchor -- four prose edits across three skill files and one free-text plan convention. NO SKILL WAS EDITED by this ticket and `skill-manager sync` was never run.

ticket.objective: A RESEARCH TICKET -- design and evidence, NO production code and NO EDITS TO ANY SKILL. The goal process spans the skills that create issues, run tickets and schedule epics, and NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM REACHES THE SCORECARD. The entire cross-skill surface is THREE SKILLS AND FOUR FILES: one cross-reference in git-epic-workflow/references/goals-and-evaluation.md, git-issue-workflow's goal-signal.md, and git-issue's SKILL.md and regression-close.md -- and spec-double-compiler's ~990 matches are its bundled copy of THIS repository's record, which must be confirmed rather than assumed. READ goal-signal.md AND regression-close.md FIRST: goal-signal machinery and a regression-close path ALREADY EXIST, and the most valuable outcome may be that the hooks are there and nothing populates them. Decide where in the lifecycle the score belongs and which seams are WRONG places; what can cross a skill boundary and what is meaningless outside the project that produced it; and how this survives a project that does not use the card, WHICH IS MOST OF THEM. DO NOT DESIGN A FRAMEWORK -- four files, and if the answer is two sentences and one field that is a better result than an architecture.
